Differential Expression and Pathway Enrichment

Chomchon Uansiri

Source: vignettes/OHMmy-differential-expression.Rmd
OHMmy-differential-expression.Rmd

Introduction

Once you have identified your cell clusters, the next step is discovering what makes them unique biologically. OHMmy automates the extraction of cluster markers, pathway enrichment (GSEA and ORA), and visualizes pseudo-bulk differential expression (DESeq2) between experimental conditions.


library(Seurat)
library(OHMmy)
library(msigdbr) # Required for pathway databases

# Load your clustered Seurat object
seurat_obj <- readRDS("data/seurat_clustered.rds")
out_dir <- "results/differential_expression/"

Part 1: Finding Top Cluster Markers

The FindTopMarkersAndHeatmap() function runs FindAllMarkers() to find the defining genes for each cluster, saves the results as a ready-to-use CSV file, and generates a heatmap of the top genes.


# 1. Set the active identity to your desired cluster resolution
Idents(seurat_obj) <- "cell_type_annotation"

# 2. Find markers and generate the heatmap
marker_results <- FindTopMarkersAndHeatmap(
  seurat_obj = seurat_obj,
  sample_name = "Cohort_A",
  output_dir_base = paste0(out_dir, "cluster_markers/"),
  plot_format = "jpg",
  onlyPos = FALSE # Set to FALSE to capture both up and down-regulated markers
)

# You can access the saved dataframe directly for the next step
gsea_input_df <- marker_results$markers

Part 2: Pathway Enrichment (GSEA & ORA)

Using the marker dataframe generated in Part 1, we can test if specific biological pathways (like the MSigDB Hallmark gene sets) are enriched in our clusters.

First, we download the Human Hallmark database:


m_t2g_hallmark <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", category = "H")[, c("gs_name", "gene_symbol")]

2.1 Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA)

GSEA evaluates the entire ranked list of genes for a cluster (both positive and negative markers) to find coordinated pathway shifts.


gsea_results <- run_global_gsea(
  GSEA_df = gsea_input_df, 
  m_t2g = m_t2g_hallmark, 
  title_prefix = "Hallmark",
  top_n_per_direction = 30, # Plot the top 30 up/down pathways per cluster
  output_dir = paste0(out_dir, "GSEA/")
)

2.2 Over-Representation Analysis (ORA)

ORA evaluates only the significant positive markers to see if they overlap significantly with known pathway gene lists.


ora_results <- run_global_ora(
  ORA_df = gsea_input_df, 
  m_t2g = m_t2g_hallmark, 
  title_prefix = "Hallmark",
  top_n_per_cluster = 30,
  output_dir = paste0(out_dir, "ORA/")
)

Part 3: Pseudo-bulk Differential Expression (DESeq2)

While FindAllMarkers() compares clusters against each other, DESeq2 compares the same cluster across different conditions (e.g., Healthy vs. Disease). OHMmy provides wrappers to visualize DESeq2 results natively.

(Note: Generating the DESeq2 res object using pseudo-bulk aggregation is assumed to be completed prior to visualization).

3.1 Volcano Plots

Visualize significant gene expression fold-changes between two conditions.


# Define genes you want highlighted on the volcano plot
highlight_genes <- c("IFNG", "GZMB", "TNF", "CX3CR1", "IL7R")

# Generate the plot for Disease vs Control
volcano_plot <- generate_volcano_trio(
  res_obj = res_Disease_vs_Control, # Your DESeq2 results object
  plot_title = "Severe Disease vs Healthy Control", 
  target_genes = highlight_genes
)

# Save the plot
ggsave(paste0(out_dir, "DESeq2/volcano_disease_vs_control.png"), 
       plot = volcano_plot, width = 20, height = 8)

3.2 Heatmaps of Differentially Expressed Genes

To visualize how the top significant genes fluctuate across individual patients, we use generate_and_save_heatmap().


# 1. Transform the count data (Required for heatmaps)
vsd_data <- DESeq2::vst(dds_object, blind = FALSE)

# 2. Setup the annotation column (e.g., Patient Condition)
anno_col <- as.data.frame(colData(dds_object)[, "disease_state", drop = FALSE])
ordered_samples <- rownames(anno_col)[order(anno_col$disease_state)]

# 3. Generate the heatmap
generate_and_save_heatmap(
  res_obj = res_Disease_vs_Control,
  comp_name = "Disease_vs_Control",
  comp_title = "Severe Disease vs Healthy Control",
  vsd_data = vsd_data,
  anno_col = anno_col,
  ordered_samps = ordered_samples,
  n_padj = 50, # Plot top 50 significant genes
  out_dir = paste0(out_dir, "DESeq2/")
)
